name: Gravite-HD
description: An ultra-dense osmium-rhenium-neutron-analog composite assembled with quantum precision to achieve a bulk density of approximately 48 g/cm³ — nearly double that of osmium and four times that of lead — by filling interstitial lattice space with stabilized heavy-element clusters that would be impossible to maintain under conventional manufacturing conditions. Gravite-HD is used where maximum mass in minimum volume is required: ballistic counterweights, radiation shielding, penetrator munitions, and structural ballast in space-limited environments. Its extreme density also provides passive radiation attenuation superior to any conventional shielding material of equivalent volume.
story_hooks: A Gravite-HD counterweight has gone missing from a Spire construction site — at 48 g/cm³, even a fist-sized piece masses over 25 kilograms, and someone carried it out without triggering any load sensors, which should have been impossible.

Crucible Industries is marketing Gravite-HD penetrators to both sides of a corporate conflict — the rounds punch through any existing armor at the tiers involved, and the body count is escalating in ways that are starting to attract unwanted regulatory attention.

A street-level fence is selling what she claims are Gravite-HD fragments from a 'crashed military drone' — the density checks out, but the crystalline structure inside doesn't match any known Crucible Industries production run.
